column2: Open the Journey menu (J) and follow the A New Beginning cards in order. They list exactly what to gather, research and craft next.
Spend skill points and Intel as soon as you get them. Unspent points do nothing.
Pick up loose rocks, ore pieces and salvage scrap as you walk. Small pieces are collected by hand; big wrecks need a Cutteray.
Map colors: green markers (shipwrecks) hold weapon and armor parts, blue (testing stations) vehicle parts, orange (sealed caves) water and gathering parts.
Research what the journey asks for first: clothing, pistol, binoculars, respawn beacon, construction kit, blood extractor, purifier, refinery.
Get the Vehicle Backup Tool early. It stores a sandbike and can recover a destroyed vehicle for Solari.
Enemy outposts hold Intel pickups marked on the map. Scout them with binoculars from a safe distance first.
Each Cutteray tier mines new ores: Mk2 carbon, Mk3 aluminum, Mk4 jasmium. If a node will not mine, your Cutteray is too low.
Keep hydration above one third for a stamina bonus, above two thirds for a bigger one. At zero you lose health.
Dew Flowers only fill you to one third and too much causes nausea. Use them to top up, not as your main water.
Carry a blood extractor and a blood sack. Every fight is a water refill.
Drinking raw blood costs max health. Put it in a Blood Purifier at your base for clean water.
Drink your stillsuit catchpockets first; they refill while you wear the suit.
Dew Reapers work best at dawn.
The world does not pause in the Escape menu. Your water keeps draining while you sit in menus.
Direct sun fills the sunstroke bar, and sunstroke speeds dehydration. Step into shadow to clear it.
Travel by night and do base chores at midday. The game itself gives this advice.
Hot regions drain water faster no matter what. Better stillsuits have more Heat Protection.
When the vibration bar turns red, a worm is close. Get onto rock immediately.
The worm threat meter does not drain while you are on sand. It only drains once you are on rock or in the air.
Cross open sand in short hops from rock to rock, by the shortest line. Never stop on sand to loot or mine.
Crouching makes as much worm threat as walking. Running only adds a third more. Dashing is much louder.
Never switch on a personal shield on open sand. It makes worm threat over 30 times faster than walking.
Suspensors and drumsand are loud too: about 13 times the threat of walking.
Watch the map for quicksand and drumsand markers. Quicksand can kill; drumsand calls the worm.
Do not stand near a spice blow when it erupts. The shockwave destroys everything nearby.
In an ornithopter, climb when a worm is near. Low flight is still vulnerable.
A thumper on open sand attracts and distracts the worm. Place it away from where you work.
Fire a survey probe from high ground to reveal the whole area: places, resources, hazards and terrain.
Use binoculars to spot outposts and set a waypoint before you walk into anything.
To leave a map you need a flying vehicle, at least 50% fuel and 30% hydration, and no passengers.
Tradepost taxi pilots fly you to another tradepost for 150 Solari or to a city for 500.
Cross to the Vermillius Gap on a sandbike, by the short flat route just northeast of Griffin's Reach.
Place a Respawn Beacon before any risky trip. Only one is active; a new one replaces the old.
When you die, your backpack drops at the Death Location marker. Go straight back; it does not last forever.
Leave valuables in base storage before risky trips. Only what you carry can drop.
A sandworm kill loses what you carry and destroys the vehicle you are in. On this server it takes your backpack.
Park inside your own claim under a roof. Vehicles outside a claim decay even when sheltered.
Never leave a ground vehicle behind when changing maps. It is destroyed; store it in the Vehicle Backup Tool first.
Vehicles burn Vehicle Fuel Cells made at a Chemical Refinery, not raw Fuel Cells. Carry a spare.
A destroyed vehicle can be rebuilt in the Vehicle Backup Tool's Recovery mode for Solari. Its cargo is lost.
Build your first base small, on rock, in Hagga Basin South. The journey later has you move it north.
Move your Sub-Fief Console inside your shelter, and feed the generator Fuel Cells to power machines and the base shield.
Fuel Cells come from scavenger camps. Put them in base storage, then process them in the generator.
Back up your base with the Base Reconstruction Tool before big moves. It keeps up to three bases.
Base gone or vehicle missing? Check the Activity Log in the Communinet tab of the Social menu.
When a sandstorm warning shows, get indoors, into a cave or a tradepost. Your shelter status shows above the water bar.
Three quick light attacks stagger. A heavy attack breaks block and gets through shields after a stagger.
Block just as the enemy swings to parry. It staggers them and gives you stamina back.
Beat shielded enemies with stagger plus heavy attack, or poison or fire, which pass through shields.
Staggered? Dash in any direction to snap out of it.
Craft Healkits from Plant Fiber, which grows everywhere. Keep a stack on your hotbar.
Holster your weapon to move faster when you are not fighting.
Take contracts from tradepost boards. Rewards that do not fit your bag can be claimed later in the Journey menu.
NPC vendors buy back at a small fraction of their price. Sell valuable items to players on the Exchange instead.
Keys: J journey, M map, I inventory, Y research, K skills, B crafting, P social, O guild, N Communinet, Enter chat.
Mark one item for Quick Swap on the loadout wheel, then double-tap Holster to switch to it.
On this server, sandstorms give about two minutes of warning and never damage buildings.
On this server, inventory volume is 10 times normal, but you still have 35 backpack slots.
On this server, type &help in chat to see which & commands you may use.
